entities.summary: Diego de Lepe, a Castilian navigator from Palos de la Frontera, embarked on a pivotal Atlantic expedition in 1499-1500, contributing to Spain's early cartographic understanding of the South American coastline. Operating within the intense geopolitical rivalry between Spain and Portugal codified by the Treaty of Tordesillas, Lepe's voyage, though less celebrated than those of contemporaries like Vicente Yáñez Pinzón and Pedro Álvares Cabral, underscored the urgency and competitive spirit driving the Age of Discovery. His efforts helped solidify Spain's claims in the nascent colonial enterprise, pushing the boundaries of known geography and influencing subsequent explorations.
